newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Fuel supplies targeted in WA industrial protest.
newsitem.headline: Fuel supplies targeted in WA industrial protest.

text.p: Fuel tanker drivers in Western Australia will stop work from midnight tonight as part of the continuing trade union protest against proposed changes to the state's industrial relations laws.
Jim McGiveron, the secretary of the Transport Workers Union said today the drivers will meet tomorrow morning to decide how long they will stay out.
"Aircraft refuellers will also attend the meeting but they will not stop work from midnight," McGiveron said.
"They will leave the job to attend and decide if they will get involved."

The protest campaign got underway with a "Day of Action" on Tuesday last week. It quickly developed into a six-day strike by a small group of power station employees that resulted in thousands of workers being stood down in industry throughout the south west of the state.

Construction workers on a number of major sites, including the new Collie Power Station, are still on strike and on Tuesday members of the Australian Manufacturing Workers Union will hold a 24-hour stoppage.

The legislation at the centre of the dispute has passed through the Legislative Assembly and is being debated in the Legislative Council where the government holds a one-seat majority until May 21 when members elected at last year's state election will take their seats.
The protest campaign is being coordinated by the peak trade union body, the Trades and Labour Council. Its secretary, Tony Cooke, said today:
"There is a determination by the Government to get the legislation through Parliament by Thursday May 15 and there is an equal determination on our part that they will fail."
